messages.content:
The test `testUnion()` in `DOMModelTest` from the `org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.dom` package failed. The test case involves executing an XPath query `"/vendor[1]/contact[4] | /vendor[1]/contact[1]"` and asserting the expected value to be "John".

The current bug report indicates that the core union operation in XPath does not sort result nodes according to document order. Specifically, for the given XPath expression `string(/MAIN/B | /MAIN/A)`, the expected result is "avalue" because the node in document order should be selected first. However, the actual value returned is "b", which is incorrect.

Looking at the test case for `testUnion()` in `DOMModelTest`, it seems to be validating different types of XPath queries but does not directly relate to the reported issue of sorting nodes according to document order in the union operation.

Given the nature of the reported bug and the provided test case, it is likely that the issue lies in the implementation of the XPath evaluation or union operation logic within the JXPath library, possibly in the handling of node set ordering during union operations.

To diagnose this issue further, it would be necessary to inspect the implementation of the XPath evaluation and union operation logic in the `org.apache.commons.jxpath` library, specifically focusing on how the union of node sets is handled to ensure the correct sorting according to document order.

Next, I will provide the best locations to fix this issue.
The corresponding issue report describes that the core union operation in XPath does not sort result nodes according to document order, leading to incorrect results. To address this, the logic related to the union operation and node set sorting in the XPath evaluation needs to be corrected.

Potential fix locations:
- `org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.dom.DOMModel.buildNodeSet(Expression, JXPathContext, Pointer)`
- `org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.NodePointer.compareNodePointers(NodePointer, NodePointer)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
